exam.experience: Recommended, not required: security administrator with two years of hands-on experience
exam.launch: CompTIA says on or around November 17, 2026

objectives.short: Threat actors and what drives them
Managing hardware, software and data assets

weeks.title: Computer and IT fundamentals
weeks.outcome: Explain how a computer system works and name the basic parts of an IT environment.

weeks.title: Networking fundamentals
weeks.outcome: Explain how devices communicate within a network and across the internet.

weeks.title: Network communication and protocols
weeks.outcome: Explain how information travels between devices and what happens when someone opens a website or remote service.

weeks.title: Operating systems and security fundamentals
weeks.outcome: Describe the technical environment that security professionals protect.

weeks.title: Domain 1: General Security Concepts
weeks.outcome: Explain core security concepts, change management and cryptographic solutions.

weeks.title: Domain 2, part 1: threats, actors and vectors
weeks.outcome: Describe threats, vulnerabilities, threat actors and how attacks reach an organization.

weeks.title: Domain 2, part 2: vulnerabilities, indicators and AI
weeks.outcome: Identify attack surfaces, read signs of malicious activity and explain AI-related threats.

weeks.title: Domain 3, part 1: architecture models and infrastructure
weeks.outcome: Compare architecture models and choose controls that protect infrastructure.

weeks.title: Domain 3, part 2: data protection and resilience
weeks.outcome: Protect data through its life cycle and plan for recovery.

weeks.title: Domain 4, part 1: controls and assets
weeks.outcome: Apply network, endpoint, application and email controls, and manage assets securely.

weeks.title: Domain 4, part 2: vulnerabilities, monitoring and identity
weeks.outcome: Run vulnerability management, understand monitoring tools and apply identity and access concepts.

weeks.title: Domain 4, part 3: automation, response and investigation
weeks.outcome: Automate safely, run incident response and use evidence in an investigation.

weeks.title: Domain 5: Security Program Management and Oversight
weeks.outcome: Explain governance, risk, third-party management, compliance, audits and awareness.

weeks.title: Complete objective review
weeks.outcome: Find and close gaps across all 27 objectives.

sessions.title: Domain 1 objective review
sessions.detail: Retake mixed questions for objectives 1.1–1.3. A score of 80% or more counts as a review pass for each objective with enough questions.

sessions.title: Domain 2 objective review
sessions.detail: Objectives 2.1–2.6, with attention to indicators of malicious activity.

sessions.title: Domain 5 review and gap plan
sessions.detail: Objectives 5.1–5.6, then open the progress dashboard and list every objective below Reviewed.

weeks.title: Mock examination and remediation
weeks.outcome: Sit a timed 90-question exam and repair what it reveals.

sessions.title: Timed mock exam A
sessions.detail: Sit it in one 90-minute block, with no notes.

sessions.title: Read every explanation
sessions.detail: Work through all explanations for wrong answers, including why your choice was tempting.

sessions.title: Remediate your weakest domain
sessions.detail: Revisit the recommended lessons, then answer your weak-area questions.

sessions.title: Remediate your next weakest domain
sessions.detail: Repeat with the next weakest objectives.

sessions.title: Performance-based practice
sessions.detail: Complete the configuration, log and sequencing exercises.

weeks.title: Final examination readiness
weeks.outcome: Show readiness through performance, not by reaching the last week.

sessions.title: Timed mock exam B
sessions.detail: A different 90 questions in one 90-minute block.

sessions.title: Ports, acronyms and cryptography
sessions.detail: Use the ports, acronym and cryptography revision sheets.

sessions.title: IAM and attack recognition
sessions.detail: Use the IAM and attack recognition sheets, then your weak-area questions.

sessions.title: Security operations and incident response
sessions.detail: Use the operations and incident response sheets, and retry any PBQ under 80%.

sessions.title: Final readiness check
sessions.detail: Compare your demonstrated performance with the readiness checklist. Extend your study if any line is not met.

modules.design: Understand how digital products communicate and depend on infrastructure.

modules.title: Threats and Vulnerabilities

modules.design: Threat-aware product flows, AI safeguards and secure interactions.

modules.title: Security Architecture
modules.security: Cloud, network architecture, data protection and resilience.
modules.design: Multi-tenant SaaS, secure product architecture and data flows.

modules.title: Security Operations
modules.security: Controls, IAM, monitoring, automation, incident response and investigation.
modules.design: Admin interfaces, permission models, security dashboards and recovery.

modules.title: Security Governance and Risk
modules.security: Governance, risk, third parties, compliance, audits and awareness.
modules.design: Privacy experiences, security requirements and vendor workflows.

modules.title: Exam Readiness
modules.security: Revision, performance-based practice and timed mock exams.
modules.design: Integrated technical and design case studies.
